g3ela-29-1-teach-morph: [curious] A throw is hiding inside this word. Projectile. Pro means forward. Ject means throw. A projectile is something thrown forward, like a snowball. Read the four words and their parts, and tap See if you were right. Then type the missing part in each box.
g3ela-29-1-teach-vocab: Be a word detective with me. Earnestly. Here's the sentence. The Lion and the Witch talked earnestly together in low voices. One, read the sentence: everyone is waiting, and worried. Two, look for word parts: earnest, l y. Three, check it. Earnestly means in a very serious way. Read how we figured out the first word. Then fill in each sentence with a word from the word bank, and tap Check My Work. Last, play the matching game.
g3ela-29-1-teach-gram: [warmly] When someone talks in a story, their words get a little house. We're home, said Mom. Quotation marks go around We're home. We're gets a capital. The comma goes inside, before the closing mark. Tap Now check your thinking. Then find the three dialogue mistakes.
g3ela-29-1-teach-spell: Big words come apart! Unbreakable. Find the root first: break. The front part is un. The end part is able. Un, break, able. Think about the questions, and tap Now name the pattern. Then sort the words.
g3ela-29-2-teach-morph: Watch one match first. Interject. Inter means between, and ject means throw. To interject is to throw your words in while someone else is talking. That's my match! Read the Remember box. Then tap a word, and tap what it means. Match all four words.
g3ela-29-2-teach-vocab: Ever seen a face so serious that nobody dared to ask a question? Stern. Aslan's face was stern. Stern means very serious, and a little strict. Now tap a word, then tap its meaning. Match all three.
g3ela-29-2-teach-gram: Find the two mistakes. come here. said Dad. Come needs a capital, because it starts the spoken words. And that period should be a comma, inside the quotation mark. Read the four sentences, and tap Now check your thinking. Then fix the paragraph.
g3ela-29-2-teach-spell: Root hunt! Lucy unlocked the door. Unlocked: un, lock, e d. Lock is the root, with parts on both ends. That one gets a tap! Read the rule. Then tap every word in the two sentences that is built from a root with parts added.
g3ela-29-2-teach-rwm: Let's try all three parts with part of a sentence from Chapter 14. They kissed his mane and his nose and his paws and his great, sad eyes. Part one, read like a reader. Lucy and Susan love Aslan, and they are saying goodbye. Part two, read like a writer. It's a list joined by and. The last one, his great, sad eyes, is the longest, so the list ends slowly. Part three, mimic. Here's mine: I hugged my dog's ears and his nose and his paws and his warm, sleepy head. Now it's your turn with the Witch's list of names. Write one sentence in each box.
g3ela-29-3-teach-morph: Snap the parts together. Ob. Ject. Object! When you object, you throw a no against an idea. Say each pair of parts out loud. Type the whole word in the box. Then tap Check My Answers.
g3ela-29-3-teach-vocab: Try each word in the blank, and keep the one that makes sense. Here's my sentence. My brother broke my cup, so he cleaned up the mess to blank. Traitor? Hmm, no. Atone? Yes! Now pick the word that fits each sentence.
g3ela-29-3-teach-gram: Be the editor. where are my boots, asked Peter. Where needs a capital, because it starts the spoken words. It's a question, so a question mark goes inside the closing mark. Read the before and after, and tap Check yourself. Then fix the line in the gray box.
g3ela-29-3-teach-spell: Let's spell one from the root. Replanted. The root is plant. Re goes on the front, and e d goes on the end. Re, plant, e d. Replanted! Read the rule. Look hard at each word, cover it, and write it. Then tap the card to check.
g3ela-29-4-teach-morph: Quick question: what does ject mean? Throw! Here's a word that's not on the dice. Trajectory. It's the path something takes when you throw it, like the curve of a ball. Say what the word part means. Then tap Roll the Dice. Say what the word means, and tap Check My Thinking. Roll all six words.
g3ela-29-4-teach-vocab: One word can carry a big idea. Traitor. At first, Edmund acts like a traitor, but in Chapter 13 his family forgives him. One word, one big idea. Now choose your word, and write your own sentence about the theme.
g3ela-29-4-teach-gram: Two passes, like an editor. its snowing, said peter. Pass one, capitals: It's and Peter. Pass two, apostrophes: it's means it is. The comma is already inside. Now do your passes, and tap every word that needs fixing.
g3ela-29-4-teach-spell: Dice roll: uncovered! Cover the front and the end. What's left? Cover! That's the root, and the parts are un and e d. Tap Roll the dice, say the root and the parts, and tap Check my answer.
